The checker independently builds W(2), confirms 30 distance rows and spectra, plus exact determinant factor identities. No existence for arbitrary (s,t) is assumed.

broader_coverage.reasoning: DeVille covers arbitrary generalized-distance matrices on distance-regular graphs and therefore already supplies stronger algorithmic coverage for s=t. For s≠t, degree on point-side is t+1 and on line-side s+1; the incidence graph fails regularity, so this theorem cannot be invoked there. The present two-fiber theorem explicitly handles that missing unequal-order class. Broader coherent-configuration literature remains a live risk.

originality.rationale: Actual searches of published mathematical findings and reviewed primary full-text material were compared by implication. DeVille 2017 covers all generalized-distance matrices in the *distance-regular* case and so covers s=t by specialization, but not s≠t where point and line degrees differ. Huang 2014 develops incidence spectra, not the simultaneous five-value positivity cone. Previously published projective-plane and generalized-hexagon results are not implications for arbitrary-radial unequal-order generalized quadrangles. New component is the exact two-fiber cone plus a sharp universal exponential cutoff and ranks across all existing (s,t). Residual coherent-configuration coverage risk is explicit.
residual_risks: Equivalent five-distance kernel PSD inequalities may appear in unindexed coherent configuration or semiregular bipartite spectral literature.

value.rationale: The motivated invariant is the full positive-definite radial covariance cone on a canonical two-fiber finite metric geometry. A complete five-parameter classification is structurally stronger than a single distance spectrum or routine one-parameter substitution; it includes unequal-order non-distance-regular and non-transitive incidence graphs, computes each eigenvalue multiplicity and rank, and yields a sharp Gaussian graph-distance admissibility cutoff with an exceptional one-dimensional kernel. These details support covariance feasibility and exact harmonic spectral calculation on generalized quadrangles.
